frames.subject: One broad low Inheritance restoration machine called a Paver, a calm road-works machine about 3 metres wide, 4 metres long and 1.6 metres tall. Wide flat continuous matte bone-white shell with very few seams and no identifiers, riding on four broad low tracked bogies tucked under a skirt, undercarriage and joints in matte ink black. A substantial articulated work head at the front: a wide horizontal screed housing carried on two ink-black hydraulic arms, a long narrow projector lens slot along its leading edge, two small muted cyan working indicator strips. Exposed ink-black mechanical service bay with pistons on the flank. Unsettling purposeful order, not a military vehicle, no red, no face

One broad low Inheritance restoration machine called a Paver, about 3 metres wide and 4 metres long, low wide wedge-shaped continuous matte bone-white body on six short ink-black wheels hidden under the body edge. At the front a heavy articulated work head like a wide road-marking and resurfacing bar, lowered on ink-black jointed arms, with a recessed projector window across its whole width and sparse muted cyan indicator lights. Ink-black exposed hydraulic joints and service ducts between the shell plates. Few seams, no markings, calm and precise, not menacing, no red, no face

One broad low Inheritance restoration machine called a Paver, a road-works machine about 3 metres wide, 4 metres long and 1.5 metres tall, flat broad matte bone-white body like a smooth paving stone, on four short stout ink-black legs ending in broad flat pads. A large front work head on a thick ink-black boom: a wide rectangular tool housing with a downward-facing projector strip and a row of tamping plates, two small muted cyan indicators. Exposed ink-black mechanical joints. Few seams, no identifiers, unsettling order, not a military vehicle, no red, no face

One elevated Inheritance observation machine called a Surveyor, about 4 metres tall. A compact matte bone-white sensor head dominated by one oversized circular lens assembly with ink-black iris shutter blades half open, a thin projector ring around the lens, sparse muted cyan indicators, carried on a tall slender ink-black telescoping mast standing on a broad stable tripod of three bone-white folded legs with ink-black joints. Continuous surfaces, few seams, no identifiers, calm and watchful, no red, no face, no eyes besides the lens

One elevated Inheritance observation machine called a Surveyor, about 4 metres tall. Muted cyan indicator ring around the lens rim. Continuous surfaces, few seams, no identifiers, unsettling stillness, no red, no face

One elevated Inheritance observation machine called a Surveyor, a tall slender machine about 4 metres high: a long ink-black mast with a bone-white counterweighted head at the top carrying an oversized lens barrel assembly with its iris fully open and a pale muted cyan glass, a small downward projector beneath the lens, the mast on a four-legged bone-white spider base with ink-black joints. Continuous matte surfaces, few seams, no identifiers, no red, no face

One narrow Inheritance restoration machine called a Collector, about 2.2 metres tall and 0.7 metres wide, a narrow continuous matte off-white upright body with very few seams and no identifiers, walking on two long ink-black jointed legs, one long precise ink-black work arm ending in a broad gripping and prying tool extended forward in a committed working pose, leaning deliberately into the work, a small muted cyan work indicator. Calm, deliberate, uncanny order, not a Union soldier, no red, no head, no face

One narrow Inheritance restoration machine called a Collector, about 2.2 metres tall, a tall slim continuous matte off-white body like a smooth narrow capsule on three ink-black jointed legs, two ink-black work arms folded close, one arm extended holding a broad flat cutting and lifting tool in a committed pose. One narrow Inheritance restoration machine called a Collector, about 2.2 metres tall and narrow, an upright continuous matte off-white body tapering at the top, moving on a compact ink-black wheeled base, with one long articulated ink-black boom arm ending in a heavy clamp-and-saw obstruction-clearing tool lowered forward as if committing to work, small muted cyan indicators. One personally adapted industrial flight pack, a jetpack worn on the back, about 70 centimetres tall: tubular gunmetal steel back frame, two clear downward thrust nozzles with heat-darkened steel bells at the bottom, two dented bone-enamel fuel cylinders between them with brass valve handwheels and braided hoses, worn brown leather shoulder straps and waist belt, one replaced rust-coloured side panel, a small round analog gauge without numbers, hand-made coalition repairs and clamps. One personally adapted industrial flight pack, a jetpack about 70 centimetres tall, seen from the rear three-quarter: a compact boxy bone-enamel engine housing with two short angled twin thrust nozzles below, two slim gunmetal fuel tanks on the sides, ember-orange valve caps, a folding control lever on a hose, worn brown leather harness straps with buckles, welded repair plates and wire wrapping. One foldable civilian-built portable automatic sentry, deployed: three splayed welded steel tripod legs with small feet, a yaw collar, a pitch cradle holding a compact practical gun receiver with a short shrouded barrel, a clearly visible side-mounted ammunition box with a feed belt, mechanical slew joints.
